title: Choose the visual world for Safar
question: The roll assigned Airport Wayfinding. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.lineage: International airport signage (ICAO pictograms, yellow-on-black direction signs, Bole terminal bilingual panels)
options.thesis: Every step the agent takes is signposted like a terminal: follow any sign to its source.
options.viewport: Charcoal gantry header; proposal on a light concourse ground; trace rail is a column of directional signs, the running step a black-on-yellow 'you are here' sign.
options.risk: If yellow spreads past the signs it reads as a construction site, not an airport.

raised.raise: One fixed price ramp: every result's price is drawn on the same shared scale.
Every flight or hotel option carries the same furniture in the same slots.
No easing: signs switch in a hard 90ms two-step, never fade.
Every tool call gets a gate number (A1, A2…) that the proposal cites.
All figures set in tabular numerals at data density.

options.label: Flight Coupon
options.lineage: Multi-part paper airline ticket coupons and agency itinerary printouts
options.thesis: The proposal issued as a ticket; each tool result a numbered coupon torn along a perforation.
options.viewport: Proposal as an issued itinerary with coupon stubs; trace as a stack of torn coupons.
options.risk: Familiar: boarding-pass UI is the most common travel-app trope.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards and one action colour reserved for whatever you can press.
options.viewport: Single column of trace cards above the proposal; one blue action colour.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads clearly, but agency staff aren't consumers, so it loses on identification.
options.risk: Generic: nothing an evaluator remembers an hour later.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Results plotted as stars, magnitude as importance.
options.viewport: Results plotted as stars on a chart.
options.case: Travel agents don't identify with star charts, and a plot hides prices.
options.risk: Pretty, but it can't be read as a quote.
options.kept: A fixed ramp carries hierarchy, so prices sit on one shared scale.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Options as a ranked roster of characters.
options.case: Undercuts trust in a pricing tool on both axes.
options.kept: Every option carries the same fixed furniture in fixed slots.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Steps as acetate leaves over hued divider boards.
options.case: Software-manual nostalgia, not travel; its layering obscures state.
options.risk: Reads as a manual, not a working desk.
options.kept: One strict motion grammar: hard two-frame steps, no easing.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything a numbered catalog entry on black.
options.case: Coded labels fight a tool that must read instantly.
options.kept: Every step gets a sequential number the output cites.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Agent output as a strobing black-and-white data field.
options.case: Spectacle over a quote; loses both axes.
options.risk: Unreadable for an agent on deadline.
options.kept: One tabular numeric voice at data density.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An AI chat app with collapsible tool-step chips, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of chats, centred conversation, tool steps as grey collapsible chips inline.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every AI demo an evaluator has already seen.
